clue.text: Where a composer may modulate for a change?

explanation.surface: A musical question about where a composer shifts key, asked for the sake of variety.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a transition is the linking passage in which a piece shifts key; in general use the word means a shift from one state to another.

clue.text: Snares supplied for jazz drums

explanation.surface: Snares are provided for a jazz drum kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Snares are devices for catching animals, and the traps is the old name for a jazz drummer's kit.

clue.text: Dismay nobody, thus mounting a horse

parts.note: to dismay someone is to appal them
nobody is nought, written as the round letter O

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting means the word for 'thus' climbs upwards, so it is read backwards

parts.note: thus means so

explanation.surface: Someone is told not to alarm anyone while climbing onto a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' turns SO into OS, since in a down entry the piece reads from the bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: An Appaloosa is a spotted breed of horse from North America.

clue.text: Favourite resort for impressing the floor

parts.note: impressing a mark into something, as with a die, is stamping it
the floor is the ground underfoot

explanation.surface: A favourite haunt chosen because it is good for stamping on the floor, perhaps by dancers.
explanation.definitionFit: A stamping ground is an idiom for the place a person habitually frequents.

clue.text: An elder's most exalted position?

parts.note: an elder looks like a senior church figure with a lofty rank, but it is the elder tree, whose highest point is meant

explanation.surface: A question about the highest rank a church elder can reach.
explanation.definitionFit: The topmost branches of an elder, a common shrub or small tree, are its highest point.

clue.text: Enchanting as Pirrip, say, when embracing sweetheart

indicators.note: embracing means the word for Pirrip's kind of person wraps round the heart of the sweet

parts.note: Philip Pirrip, called Pip, is the orphan hero of Dickens's Great Expectations, so he is an example of an orphan
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: Pip of Great Expectations is charming when he hugs his beloved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks Pirrip as an example of a parentless child, not a word to use.
explanation.definitionFit: Orphean means like the music of Orpheus, whose playing could charm beasts and stones, so it is a poetic word for spellbinding.

clue.text: Pitcher runs after sheep

indicators.note: after means the runs abbreviation is placed following the female sheep

parts.note: a ewe is a female sheep
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: In baseball or cricket a pitcher sprints off after some sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitcher' suggests a baseball player, but it is a jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large jug with a wide mouth, once used to hold washing water.

clue.text: Cetacean cry of woe, heard by many

indicators.note: heard means the word is spoken; by many signals that most, though not all, speakers say the two alike

parts.note: a wail is a long cry of grief

explanation.surface: A whale's mournful cry is heard by a great many listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by many' allows for speakers, some Scots for example, who sound the WH differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Cetaceans are the order of marine mammals that includes the large sea creature with a blowhole.

clue.text: Story-teller roughed up near court

indicators.note: roughed up means the letters of the two following words are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A storyteller is beaten up near a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is someone skilled at telling anecdotes entertainingly.

clue.text: Striped creature responsible for King Edward's destruction

definitions.text: Striped creature responsible for King Edward's destruction

parts.words: Striped creature responsible for King Edward's destruction
parts.note: King Edward reads as a monarch who was assassinated, but it is a variety of potato, devoured by a striped beetle

explanation.surface: A striped animal is blamed for killing a King Edward of England.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is a popular British potato variety.
explanation.definitionFit: This yellow-and-black striped beetle is a notorious pest that strips the leaves of potato plants.

clue.text: A soft sort of pudding put together to satisfy

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft
pease pudding is a British dish of boiled split peas

explanation.surface: Someone assembles a gentle kind of dessert to please the diners.
explanation.walkthrough: Pease pudding is a traditional British dish of mashed split peas.
explanation.definitionFit: To appease is to pacify someone by giving them what they demand.

clue.text: Dull girl appearing in small photograph

indicators.note: appearing in means the girl's name is placed inside the word for a picture

parts.note: pic is a short, informal word for a photograph
Rosa is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A boring girl turns up in a little snapshot.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosaic means matter-of-fact and lacking imagination, like plain prose.

clue.text: Sailor takes tailless bird to the compound

parts.note: an old salt is an experienced sailor

indicators.note: tailless means the bird's name loses its last letter

parts.note: the petrel is a seabird

explanation.surface: A sailor carries a bird with no tail to the enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' looks like an enclosed yard, but it is a chemical compound.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre is potassium nitrate, a chemical used in gunpowder and for curing meat.

clue.text: Main key found in old vessel

indicators.note: found in means the musical key letter is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: a can is a container
E is one of the musical keys

explanation.surface: An important musical key is discovered in an ancient pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is an old poetic term for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a literary word for the high seas, as in the Spanish Main.

clue.text: Disdain to orchestrate music with final note altered

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for writing music is a note, E, and it is changed for another letter

parts.note: to score a piece is to arrange it for instruments

explanation.surface: A conductor scorns orchestrating music when the last note has been changed.
explanation.walkthrough: The final E of SCORE is a musical note; it is swapped for N.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorn and disdain are synonyms for contempt.

clue.text: Security for Peter the painter? Not quite

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe

indicators.note: not quite means the painter's name is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: Francesco Guardi was an eighteenth-century Venetian painter

explanation.surface: A question about protection for an artist called Peter the Painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter the Painter was a notorious anarchist of London's 1911 Siege of Sidney Street, which gives the surface its colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A safeguard is a measure that protects, so it gives security.

clue.text: Two sorts of wood used in the plant

parts.note: pine is a softwood timber
apple is a fruitwood used in carving and turning

explanation.surface: Two kinds of timber are used in building the factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a factory, but it is the tropical plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The pineapple is a tropical plant of the bromeliad family, grown for its fruit.

clue.text: Experimental angle for a nurse's escort?

parts.note: a pilot scheme is an experimental trial run
to angle is to fish

explanation.surface: A trial approach for whoever accompanies a nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: The nurse is the nurse shark, which pilot fish swim alongside.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilot fish swim with sharks such as the nurse shark, apparently accompanying them.

clue.text: Corrupt language of garbled RAF signal

indicators.note: garbled means the letters of the air force message are mixed up

explanation.surface: Corrupted wording in an RAF signal that has been scrambled.
explanation.definitionFit: Franglais is French spoiled by too many English borrowings, a mongrel tongue.

clue.text: Appendices amplify article on design

indicators.note: on means the article comes after the word for design

parts.note: to amplify a statement is to add to it
design can mean purpose, an end in view
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Appendices enlarge a piece of writing about design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like a piece of writing, but it is the grammatical article A.
explanation.definitionFit: Addenda are items added at the end of a book, much like supplements.

clue.text: Distrust American political leader joining breakaway group

indicators.note: joining means the other pieces go into the middle of the breakaway group's word

parts.note: a sect is a group that has split from a larger body

indicators.note: the leader of political is its first letter

explanation.surface: Doubting a US politician who joins a splinter faction.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspect someone is to doubt their honesty.

clue.text: Some women may resent his good looks

definitions.text: Some women may resent his good looks

parts.words: Some women may resent his good looks
parts.note: good looks reads as handsomeness, but it means the long hard stares of a man leering at women

explanation.surface: Some women resent a man for being handsome.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who leers at people is one who stares at them lecherously.

clue.text: Verve displayed in August or September

indicators.note: displayed in means the letters are on view inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Energy shown in late summer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty enjoyment and energy.

clue.text: Sound transfixes dog

indicators.note: sound means the word is said aloud and the entry is what it sounds like

parts.note: to spit meat is to pierce it on a skewer, so transfixes is spits

explanation.surface: A noise freezes a dog in its tracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' and 'transfixes' read as a noise startling the dog; in fact 'Sound' is the sound-alike signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The spitz is a breed of dog with a pointed muzzle and curled tail.

clue.text: Irritable characters Pepys cited — only one English

indicators.note: the letters, or characters, of the diarist's name and the next word are rearranged
only one means that of the two letters E in the fodder only one is kept

explanation.surface: Bad-tempered figures that Pepys mentioned, only one of them English.
explanation.walkthrough: PEPYS CITED has two Es; dropping one E (English) leaves the nine letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyspeptic literally means suffering indigestion, and by extension it means bad-tempered.

clue.text: Inexpensive headgear worn by an ambassador

indicators.note: worn by means the ambassador's title goes inside the headgear, as a head goes in a hat

parts.note: a cap is a piece of headgear
HE stands for His Excellency, the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: A cut-price hat is worn by a diplomat.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap means costing little.

clue.text: Scene of a noted bridge party in Provence?

definitions.text: Scene of a noted bridge party in Provence?

parts.words: Scene of a noted bridge party in Provence
parts.note: bridge party suggests a card game, but it is dancing on the famous bridge of the French song Sur le pont

explanation.surface: Asks where a famous card evening took place in southern France.
explanation.definitionFit: The French folk song has people dancing on the old bridge of this Provençal city.

clue.text: Wind net out to port

indicators.note: out means the word net is put into disorder

parts.note: port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A fisherman winds his net out towards the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: To entwine is to twist together, which is to wind.

clue.text: Some females sound as if they are half asleep

indicators.note: sound means the word for the female deer is spoken aloud

parts.note: does are female deer, rabbits or hares

explanation.surface: Some women sound drowsy.
explanation.definitionFit: To doze is to sleep lightly.

clue.text: Bold soldier's first to cheer the ironclad

annotationWithheld.why: Bold soldier's first to cheer the ironclad (10): HIP (cheer) and B (bold) are visible, but no parse of 'soldier's first' and 'the' gives ATTLES; the scan prints the clue the same.
annotationWithheld.clue: Bold soldier's first to cheer the ironclad
